CS2-H-01.note: Deciding span: 'peculiar enough to account for the restriction without help' - a range that needs nothing further said is self-explanatory. B 'anomalous' is the live trap because 'peculiar' sits in the same sentence, but it is killed twice: the sentence supplies an explanation rather than a puzzle, and the trials 'complicated that view' only if the view was that no more needed saying.

CS2-H-02.note: I DISAGREE WITH THE FILE KEY (file says C 'calculated'). The connectives put the blank on the side the evidence overturns: 'and the manuscripts ENCOURAGE the description: whole passages are struck through, and the replacements are entered in a hurried hand.' A hurried hand encourages 'impulsive', not 'calculated'; and 'Yet every excision removes a phrase... singled out for praise' is then the contrast that reveals system. Under the file key the sentence asserts that hurried handwriting encourages calling revisions calculated, and 'Yet' introduces evidence FOR the blank rather than against it - both connectives invert. C is only reachable by ignoring 'encourage' and 'Yet' and answering 'what were the revisions really?' Flagged second_defensible because as written both C and D can be argued and the wording that fails to separate them is 'the manuscripts encourage the description'.

CS2-H-03.note: Deciding span: 'blocks that held policies were paced out and checked twice a year, while blocks that held none were sketched from the end of the street' - detail varies by block, so unevenly distributed. No distractor survives: nothing is falsified, the paced blocks are verified, and nothing erodes (the sketch was coarse from the start, not degraded).

CS2-H-04.note: Deciding span: 'every table in the appendix reproduces what the authors say it does' - the direct complement of misreporting. D 'overstates' is the strong trap because the second sentence is entirely about overstatement, but the blank is the charge the text calls 'unfounded', and overstatement is the charge the text says is founded; picking D makes the passage contradict itself in two clauses.

CS2-H-05.note: Split is a register judgement, not a passage fact. The since-clause - 'accept material from any donor and set no ceiling on how many samples of one variety they will hold' - reads equally well as EXHAUSTIVE (A): accepting from everyone and capping nothing is exactly how a policy of total coverage would be described, and 'The catalogue records something NARROWER' is a scope word that points at coverage, i.e. at A. The only thing favouring D is that duplicates of one variety add no coverage, which is a lexical inference a reader need not make. Worse, the file's explanation eliminates A with 'two thirds of the holdings come from four sources' - that is the corrective clause, which by construction contradicts whatever the blank says, so it cannot separate candidates. C 'opportunistic' also partly survives ('accept whatever arrives'); it is ruled out only by the author's gloss that a standing rule is not opportunism.

CS2-H-06.note: Deciding span: 'a fact that the defense had already conceded in writing before the term opened.' B 'a concession' is defensible on a natural reading - the word 'conceded' is right there - and is ruled out only by the second feature 'already... before the term opened': a concession already made in writing cannot be made again by silence, so what the silence saves is effort. The contrast term is 'exhaustion' (a state), and the blank must name a purposeful alternative.

CS2-H-07.note: Deciding span: 'so a reader can follow the disagreement from session to session.' The sentence is deliberately balanced - the second half ('never learns why either camp held the view it did') is genuine support for C 'unintelligible' - but only D survives the whole sentence: traceability is untouched by the missing reasoning, whereas 'unintelligible' is flatly contradicted by the reader being able to follow it. B 'contentious' fails on the verb 'render' (minutes do not make a dispute contentious).

CS2-H-08.note: Deciding span: 'This batch... differed from itself by less than the modern specification allows' - a measurement of internal consistency, which is what 'uniform' asserts and what 'unremarkable' does not. B is defensible on a natural reading (it is the paradigm of faint praise, and D 'serviceable' is faint the same way), and is ruled out only by the second feature 'until one notices what it EXCLUDES': the mechanism needs a word whose meaning rules something out, and only 'uniform' rules out the batch-to-batch unpredictability of the second sentence. Note the last sentence also makes the iron literally remarkable.

CS2-H-09.note: Sentence 2 makes the elevation claim, sentence 3 measures it: 'the LOWEST sites lose more than half of each year's accumulation.' A is the near-miss but names the wrong target - the opening claim is about burial RATES, and nothing in the text disputes the rate; what is qualified is the inference drawn from it. C fails because sentence 3 is a result, not a hypothesis (sentence 2 is the hypothesis).

CS2-H-10.note: Deciding span: 'each of the eleven proved to have taken water from the pump by a route he had not anticipated' - the apparent exceptions dissolved. B requires the limit to be left unresolved, which the same clause forecloses.

CS2-H-11.note: Deciding span: 'nothing has been found wrong with the reasoning that produced the old account' - explicitly contradicts A's 'argues that the method behind the old account was unsound'. B invents two competing explanations; C invents a prediction.

CS2-H-12.note: Sentence 2 ('granted the charge and declined to act on it') is the position; sentences 3-4 give the serial-run evidence explaining it. B inverts it (she declined to revise), C misreads it as a restatement of the complaint, D reverses the order.

CS2-H-13.note: Deciding span: 'the two figures are not in competition' - which is what follows from the review's finding of two different definitions. A is the strongest wrong answer and reads plausibly off the first clause alone ('Neither definition is wrong'), but it needs the review to have failed to determine something, whereas the review determined the cause; and 'not in competition' denies there was a correct measurement to identify. D fails because the closing sentence states the cost rather than disputing it.

CS2-H-14.note: Deciding span: 'The same wingspan turns up in species that hover... and in species that cannot hover at all' - the opener clears wing size out of the way so the shoulder joint can be named. A misattributes: the high-speed film established the joint's rotation, not the negative claim about wingspan, which comes from the wingspan comparison. C fails because no two named species are compared throughout.

CS2-H-15.note: Four movements match B exactly: table described, 'The table is not consistent', 'Later editions reprinted it unchanged for eighty years', 'The likeliest explanation is that nobody used it as we would'. D is the live alternative because 'each single row is accurate' does defend the table, but D also requires the text to explain how a CHARGE arose, and the text raises the defect itself and explains why nobody noticed. A fails on 'traces the harm' - the point is there was none.

CS2-H-16.note: Deciding span: 'a range wide enough that the growth reported in two of the last five years falls inside it' - quantifies the problem and shows it swamps the reported signal. B inverts the order (the cause is in sentence 2). A's 'still usable' belongs to sentence 4 ('Nobody proposes discarding the counts'), not to this sentence. D invents an auditors' recommendation.

CS2-H-17.note: C is the only option covering both of Text 2's prongs - 'Those are also the hospitals with the fewest vacancies' (selection) and 'a unit held by one nurse for twelve hours has fewer witnesses' (recording artifact). B overstates into a blanket denial Text 2 never makes; A imports fatigue, absent from both texts; D turns an observation into a recommendation. passage_needed false: C is the only confound-shaped option, and the confound shape is the key in all eight cross-text items.

CS2-H-18.note: Deciding span: 'the carbon that leaves the surface layer of a plowed field turns up again at forty to sixty centimeters, below where the corers stop.' C is directly contradicted by 'Plowing does not destroy carbon; it moves it.' A and B raise issues Text 2 never touches. Guessable from the options: D is the only one that attacks the measurement rather than the world.

CS2-H-19.note: Deciding span: 'A policy that helps chiefly the unaffiliated newcomer is worth having. It is not the policy the journals believe they have adopted' - grant plus unevenness. D is the nice trap but points the wrong way: 'In a small field a reviewer can often name the author' makes concealment WEAKER in small fields, so the effect would be smaller there, not larger. C is contradicted by the effect vanishing when the policy is dropped.

CS2-H-20.note: Deciding span: 'the range across the structure settles well below the range measured in the open channel.' B merely restates Text 1's own scaling law rather than answering it; A raises engineering strength, absent from Text 2; D recommends, and Text 2 recommends nothing.

CS2-H-21.note: Deciding span: 'not at all in two reaches where elk numbers fell just as sharply but no dams were built' - the controlled counterexample to the predator-to-plant chain. D reverses the dating Text 2 actually supports; B and C assert things Text 2 never claims (it does not dispute elk browsing at all).

CS2-H-22.note: Deciding span: 'an evenly spread error rate on held-out material tells you nothing about the error it will make here' - concede the record, deny its reach. D is the overreach trap: 'tells you nothing' is agnostic about who wrote the will, so Text 2 cannot conclude the nephew did not. C contradicts Text 2, which grants the features are legible and blames the writing conditions.

CS2-H-23.note: Deciding span: 'A patron who once renewed a novel twice contributed three to the print figure and now contributes one to the electronic figure.' A is contradicted by 'the number of distinct borrowers flat across the whole period'; D would concede the rise is real, which is what Text 2 denies; C is an absurd blanket denial.

CS2-H-24.note: Deciding span: 'nothing in the design separates what the parents transmitted from what the site supplied' - D is close to a paraphrase of it. A is an absurd denial, B a prediction Text 2 does not make, C a recommendation that would repeat the confound.
